title: The prophets flee to Com
summary: In Com’s days, many prophets foretold destruction unless the people repented. The people rejected them and sought to destroy them, so they fled to Com for protection. They prophesied to Com, and he was blessed for the remainder of his days.

explicit_facts.text: Many prophets prophesied destruction unless the people repented, turned to the Lord, and forsook murder and wickedness.
The people rejected the prophets and sought to destroy them; the prophets fled to Com for protection.
The prophets prophesied many things to Com, and he was blessed for the remainder of his days.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The prophets may be shown approaching Com after fleeing to him.
unspecified_visual_details: The location, clothing, and physical appearances are unspecified.

narration.text: And there came also in the days of Com many prophets
the prophets were rejected by the people, and they fled unto Com for protection
And they prophesied unto Com many things

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Moroni narrates these events; the prophets’ words are not supplied as direct speech.
Com’s blessing over the remainder of his days is reported, not a single visible event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the prophesied destruction as occurring.
Do not invent the prophets’ spoken words or a visible manifestation of Com’s blessing.

title: War in the land
summary: Com lives to old age and begets Shiblom, who reigns after him. Shiblom’s brother rebels, and a great war begins throughout the land.

explicit_facts.text: Com lived to a good old age and begot Shiblom, who reigned in his stead.
Shiblom’s brother rebelled against him, and an exceedingly great war began throughout the land.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The rebellion and the beginning of war may be shown as conflict among unnamed people.
unspecified_visual_details: The combatants’ identities, the location, and the appearance of the war are not specified.

narration.text: there began to be an exceedingly great war in all the land

prohibited_inventions: Do not assign names or biographies to the combatants.

title: The prophets are put to death
summary: Shiblom’s brother orders the prophets who foretold destruction put to death. Calamity fills the land amid their warning of a great curse and destruction unless the people repent.

explicit_facts.text: Shiblom’s brother caused all prophets who prophesied the people’s destruction to be put to death.
There was great calamity in the land; the prophets had testified of a great curse and destruction unless the people repented of wickedness.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The order to put the prophets to death may be shown without depicting graphic injury.
unspecified_visual_details: The manner and place of the executions, and the details of the calamity, are unspecified.

narration.text: all the prophets who prophesied of the destruction
there was great calamity in all the land

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The foretold curse and destruction are presented as the prophets’ testimony; do not stage them as a distinct supernatural appearance.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict heaps of bones or specific disasters as events not explicitly narrated here.

title: Destruction in Shiblom’s days
summary: The people do not heed the Lord’s voice. Wars, contentions, famines, and pestilences occur, bringing great destruction in Shiblom’s days.

explicit_facts.text: The people did not heed the Lord’s voice because of wicked combinations; wars, contentions, famines, and pestilences led to great destruction in Shiblom’s days.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A devastated landscape may suggest the reported destruction without adding a specific disaster.
unspecified_visual_details: The people shown, the setting, and the visual form of the famines, pestilences, and destruction are unspecified.

narration.text: there began to be wars and contentions in all the land

prohibited_inventions: Do not portray metaphorical language as a separately narrated supernatural event.

title: The people repent
summary: The people begin to repent of their iniquity, and the Lord has mercy on them as they do.

explicit_facts.text: The people began to repent, and the Lord had mercy on them insofar as they did.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The people may be shown in a posture of repentance.
unspecified_visual_details: No specific act of repentance, setting, or visible manifestation of mercy is described.

narration.text: the people began to repent of their iniquity

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Mercy is stated, but no visible appearance or miracle is described.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a divine figure or a specific miraculous sign.

title: Shiblom slain; Seth captive
summary: Shiblom is slain. Seth is taken into captivity and remains captive throughout his life.

explicit_facts.text: Shiblom was slain.
Seth was brought into captivity and dwelt in captivity all his days.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The capture of Seth may be shown without depicting graphic injury.
unspecified_visual_details: The circumstances of Shiblom’s death, the identity of the captors, and the place of captivity are unspecified.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent how Shiblom was slain.

title: Ahah’s reign
summary: Ahah obtains the kingdom and reigns over the people all his days. His iniquity causes much bloodshed, and his days are few.

explicit_facts.text: Ahah, described as someone's son, obtained the kingdom and reigned over the people all his days.
Ahah's iniquity caused much bloodshed, and his days were few.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Ahah may be depicted as a ruler; the bloodshed may be suggested without depicting a specific incident.
unspecified_visual_details: The identity of Ahah's parent, his appearance, the location, and the circumstances of the bloodshed are not specified in this verse.

narration.text: Ahah, his son, did obtain the kingdom; and he did reign over the people all his days. And he did do all manner of iniquity in his days, by which he did cause the shedding of much blood; and few were his days.

prohibited_inventions: Do not name Ahah's parent from this verse alone.
Do not invent specific victims, battles, or a cause of Ahah's short life.

title: Ethem and the prophets
summary: Ethem, a descendant of Ahah, obtains the kingdom and acts wickedly. Many prophets warn the people to repent or be destroyed; the people harden their hearts, and the prophets mourn and withdraw.

explicit_facts.text: Ethem, a descendant of Ahah, obtained the kingdom and did wickedly.
Many prophets prophesied that the Lord would destroy the people unless they repented.
The people hardened their hearts and would not heed the prophets; the prophets mourned and withdrew from among them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The prophets may be shown withdrawing from the people after being rejected.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting, appearance of the prophets, and details of Ethem’s rule are unspecified.

narration.text: the prophets mourned and withdrew from among the people

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The threatened destruction is a prophecy, not an event occurring in this scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the foretold destruction as already happening.

title: Moron reigns
summary: Ethem executes judgment wickedly throughout his days and begets Moron. Moron reigns after him and does wickedly before the Lord.

explicit_facts.text: Ethem executed judgment in wickedness all his days and begot Moron.
Moron reigned in Ethem’s stead and did wickedly before the Lord.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Ethem and Moron may be shown as rulers in distinct moments of succession.
unspecified_visual_details: Their appearance, the acts of judgment, and the setting are unspecified.

narration.text: Moron did reign in his stead

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent particular judgments or acts of wickedness.

title: Rebellion against Moron
summary: A rebellion arises because of a secret combination built to gain power and gain. A mighty man gives battle to Moron, overthrows half the kingdom, and maintains that half for many years.

explicit_facts.text: A rebellion arose because of a secret combination built to get power and gain.
A mighty man gave battle to Moron, overthrew half the kingdom, and maintained it for many years.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The battle may be shown between Moron’s forces and the mighty man’s forces.
unspecified_visual_details: The mighty man’s name, the participants’ identities, and the battle’s setting are unspecified.

narration.text: there arose a rebellion among the people

prohibited_inventions: Do not name or assign a biography to the mighty man or the unnamed groups.

title: Moron regains the kingdom
summary: Moron overthrows the mighty man and obtains the kingdom again.

explicit_facts.text: Moron overthrew the mighty man and obtained the kingdom again.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The overthrow may be shown as a battle or the immediate aftermath of the struggle.
unspecified_visual_details: The manner and place of the overthrow are unspecified.
prohibited_inventions: Do not add a specific battle tactic or outcome beyond Moron regaining the kingdom.

title: Another mighty man takes the kingdom
summary: Another mighty man, descended from the brother of Jared, overthrows Moron and obtains the kingdom. Moron lives in captivity for the rest of his days and begets Coriantor.

explicit_facts.text: Another mighty man arose, a descendant of the brother of Jared.
He overthrew Moron and obtained the kingdom; Moron dwelt in captivity for the rest of his days and begot Coriantor.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The overthrow and Moron’s captivity may be represented in separate visual beats within the succession.
unspecified_visual_details: The mighty man’s identity, appearance, and the place of captivity are unspecified.

narration.text: he did overthrow Moron and obtain the kingdom

prohibited_inventions: Do not identify this mighty man as the brother of Jared; the text says he was a descendant.

title: Coriantor in captivity
summary: Coriantor dwells in captivity all his days. In his days, prophets call the people to repent and warn of destruction and of another people being brought to possess the land. The people reject their words because of their secret society and wicked abominations.

explicit_facts.text: Coriantor dwelt in captivity all his days.
In Coriantor’s days, many prophets prophesied great and marvelous things and called the people to repent, warning of destruction if they did not.
The prophets said the Lord God would bring another people to possess the land by his power, after the manner he brought their fathers.
The people rejected the prophets’ words because of their secret society and wicked abominations.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Prophetic teaching may be shown as the prophets addressing people in a supported setting.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting, the people’s identities, and the future people’s appearance are unspecified.

narration.text: Coriantor dwelt in captivity all his days
they did reject all the words of the prophets

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The prophecy of another people is reported speech and does not establish that they are present in this scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the prophesied destruction or arrival of another people as occurring here.

title: Ether is born
summary: Coriantor begets Ether and dies, having dwelt in captivity all his days.

explicit_facts.text: Coriantor begot Ether and died after dwelling in captivity all his days.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Coriantor and Ether may be shown in a single moment representing Ether’s birth.
unspecified_visual_details: The circumstances and place of Ether’s birth and Coriantor’s death are unspecified.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the separate events of Ether’s birth and Coriantor’s death as occurring simultaneously.
